title: What denominator fits both?
text: The denominators are 6 and 4. Their least common multiple is 12, same as in an addition problem. Subtraction uses the same preparation. A common mistake is to subtract the denominators. How many twelfths is $$\frac{5}{6}$$? That is, what numerator do you get when you multiply 5 by $$12 \div 6$$?

title: Rewrite the fraction you subtract
text: $$\frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{12}$$. You will subtract those 3 twelfths from 10 twelfths. What is $$10 - 3$$?

title: Worked solution
text: $$\frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{10}{12} - \frac{3}{12} = \frac{7}{12}$$. Common mistake: $$\frac{5 - 1}{6 - 4} = \frac{4}{2}$$, which is a different number. General rule: use a common denominator, then subtract numerators and keep the denominator.
